description: How web applications are attacked and defended: injection, cross-site scripting, broken authentication and session management, access-control flaws, server-side request forgery and file attacks, and the defences of input handling, output encoding and secure headers. Practised against deliberately vulnerable applications running on isolated virtual machines in the browser, so every attack and fix is carried out hands-on and safely.
modelledOn: Stuttard and Pinto, The Web Application Hacker's Handbook
OWASP Top Ten and OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
outcomes: Explain the client-server web model and map an application's attack surface.
Find and exploit injection flaws including SQL and command injection and then fix them.
Detect and prevent cross-site scripting and cross-site request forgery.
Analyse authentication, session and access-control flaws and design correct controls.
Exploit and mitigate server-side request forgery and unsafe file upload and inclusion.
Harden an application with validation, output encoding, secure headers and a sound configuration.

units.title: The web platform and its attack surface
topics: HTTP and HTTPS, requests, responses, methods, status codes and headers as an attacker sees them
The browser security model: the same-origin policy, cookies, storage and the DOM
Where trust boundaries lie: client, network, server, database and third-party services
Mapping an application: spidering, parameters, entry points and hidden functionality
Setting up an intercepting proxy and a deliberately vulnerable app on an isolated virtual machine

units.title: How web applications are attacked
topics: The OWASP Top Ten as a map of common risks and how it is used
Trust and tainted data: never trusting input from the client
Threat modelling a feature such as a mobile-money top-up form
The economics of attacks on small-business and cafe-hosted sites in Ghana
Reading an application's behaviour through error messages and timing

units.title: Injection attacks
topics: SQL injection: in-band, blind and error-based; extracting and modifying data
Exploiting a login bypass and data exfiltration against a lab database
Command, LDAP and NoSQL injection; the common root cause of mixing code and data
Defences: parameterised queries and prepared statements, least-privilege database accounts
Input validation and allow-listing as defence in depth

units.title: Cross-site scripting
topics: Reflected, stored and DOM-based cross-site scripting and their impact
Stealing sessions and performing actions as the victim; keylogging a form
Context-aware output encoding for HTML, attributes, JavaScript and URLs
Content Security Policy and trusted types; sanitising rich input
Cross-site request forgery: tokens, same-site cookies and re-authentication

units.title: Authentication and session flaws
topics: Credential handling: hashing and salting, password policy, and the weakness of SMS codes against SIM-swap
Flaws in login: user enumeration, weak reset flows, missing lockout and multi-factor
Session management: generation, transport, fixation, hijacking and timeout
Secure cookie attributes and token-based sessions
Account-recovery abuse and safe re-authentication for sensitive actions

units.title: Access control flaws
topics: Vertical and horizontal privilege escalation
Insecure direct object references and broken function-level authorisation
Exploiting an identifier to read another user's wallet or records in a lab app
Designing enforced server-side authorisation and deny-by-default
Multi-tenant isolation and testing access control systematically

units.title: Server-side request forgery and file attacks
topics: Server-side request forgery: reaching internal services and cloud metadata; blind variants
Unrestricted file upload leading to code execution; content-type and extension pitfalls
Local and remote file inclusion and path traversal
Insecure deserialisation and XML external entity attacks in brief
Defences: allow-lists, network egress restriction, safe storage and rendering of uploads

units.title: Defences and secure headers
topics: A layered defence: validation, encoding, parameterisation, authorisation and logging
Security headers: HSTS, Content Security Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame controls and referrer policy
Secure configuration: TLS, cookie flags, CORS and error handling that does not leak
Dependency and supply-chain risk; keeping components patched
A web application firewall as a stopgap, not a cure

units.title: Building and testing a secure application
topics: Secure development lifecycle: requirements, design review, testing and verification against the ASVS
Automated and manual testing with OWASP ZAP and Burp Suite
Triaging and fixing a backlog of findings for a resource-constrained team
Capstone: attack a vulnerable application, then remediate it and prove the fixes hold

schedule.title: HTTP, browsers and trust boundaries
schedule.exercise: Take a web page load and list every request, header and cookie involved, then draw the trust boundaries between the browser, network, server, database and third-party services.

tasks.title: Send GET, POST and a malformed request to a local test server with a script and record the status code and headers of each response
Demonstrate the same-origin policy by loading two local origins and showing which script access succeeds and which is blocked by the browser
Draw a trust-boundary diagram for a school portal with CDN, payment gateway and database, and mark where input must be validated

schedule.title: Mapping an application and setting up the lab
schedule.exercise: Write a lab safety checklist for an isolated testing setup, and map all entry points of a practice app into a table of parameters, methods and roles.

tasks.title: Start a deliberately vulnerable app on an isolated lab VM, check it is unreachable from outside the lab network, and confirm the proxy sees its traffic
Write a script that crawls a local practice app and lists all pages, forms and parameters it finds in a table
Find three hidden or unlinked endpoints in a practice app by comparing a wordlist scan with the linked pages, and report each with its risk

schedule.title: The OWASP Top Ten and the attacker's view
schedule.exercise: Map ten vulnerabilities from a given scan report to OWASP Top Ten categories, and threat model a mobile-money top-up form listing the data an attacker could tamper with.

tasks.title: Match ten described flaws to the right OWASP Top Ten category and justify each match, scored against the rubric
Modify hidden form fields and cookies on a practice app to show the server wrongly trusts client data, and patch the server check
Infer a hidden user list from error messages and response timing of a login form in the lab, and fix the form to respond identically

schedule.title: SQL injection in the lab
schedule.exercise: Explain the root cause shared by SQL, command and NoSQL injection, and write the vulnerable and the corrected versions of one login query.

tasks.title: Trigger an error-based SQL injection in the lab app login with a single quote and record the database error that leaks the query structure
Use a login bypass and a union query against the lab database to list the users table, and record the exact payloads and results
Exploit a command injection in a lab ping tool, then fix it with an allow-list and verify the original payloads are now rejected

schedule.title: Defending against injection
schedule.exercise: Convert four vulnerable queries to parameterised form, define a least-privilege database account for the web app, and write allow-list rules for three input fields.

tasks.title: Rewrite a login query with a prepared statement and show the earlier injection payloads now return no rows and no errors
Create a database user limited to select and insert on two tables, connect the app with it, and show a drop-table payload now fails
Add allow-list validation to five form fields of a lab app, then run 40 hostile and 40 valid inputs and report false accepts and rejects

schedule.title: Cross-site scripting and output encoding
schedule.exercise: For reflected, stored and DOM-based XSS, describe where the payload travels, what it can do to a logged-in user, and which output encoding blocks it.

tasks.title: Trigger a reflected XSS in a lab search page with an alert payload, then show how the same input is shown when properly encoded
Show in the lab how a stored XSS payload could read a session cookie to a test collector, and then protect the cookie with HttpOnly
Apply correct encoding for HTML body, attribute, JavaScript and URL contexts in a template, and pass 12 payloads that previously executed

schedule.title: CSP and request forgery
schedule.exercise: Write a Content Security Policy for a page with one external script host and no inline scripts, and describe how a CSRF token and SameSite cookie together stop a forged transfer.

tasks.title: Add a Content Security Policy header to a lab page and show an injected inline script is blocked and logged in the console
Forge a cross-site money transfer request against the lab bank, then add an anti-CSRF token and show the forged request is rejected
Sanitise rich text comments with an allow-list of tags and attributes, and test 20 bypass payloads to confirm none execute

schedule.title: Authentication and session management
schedule.exercise: Review a login, reset and session design for flaws, and write a safe password reset flow as numbered steps, including the controls that protect each step.

tasks.title: Hash 10 passwords with salted bcrypt in Python, time the work factor, and compare with the speed of cracking unsalted hashes of a small list
Find user enumeration, missing lockout and a predictable reset token in a lab login, and patch each so the faults no longer reproduce
Demonstrate session fixation in a lab app, then regenerate the session ID at login, set Secure and HttpOnly flags, and add idle timeout

schedule.title: Access control flaws
schedule.exercise: Design an authorisation scheme for a wallet app with customer, agent and admin roles, listing each endpoint's rule and a test that would catch a missing check.

tasks.title: Show horizontal escalation by changing an account number in a lab URL to view another user's profile, and record the evidence
Exploit an identifier in a lab wallet API to read another user's balance, then add an ownership check and prove the exploit now fails
Write an automated test that logs in as three roles and tries every endpoint, then reports any route that grants access it should deny

schedule.title: SSRF, file uploads and inclusion
schedule.exercise: Explain how a URL fetch feature, an image upload and a file path parameter can each become a route to the server's internals, and the single control that best stops each.

tasks.title: Read an unintended file in the lab app through a path traversal in a download parameter, then fix it by resolving and checking the path
Upload a disguised script to a lab app that checks only the extension, show it is accepted, and fix the checks to validate type and rename the file
Use an SSRF in a lab URL preview to reach an internal-only service, then block it with an allow-list and verify internal addresses fail

schedule.title: Deserialisation, XXE and their defences
schedule.exercise: Describe how an XML parser can be tricked into reading a local file and how an untrusted serialised object can run code, and list the safe configuration for each.

tasks.title: Parse a provided XML document with external entities enabled and show it reads a local lab file, then disable entities and re-run
Exploit an unsafe deserialisation in a lab service with a harmless marker payload, then replace it with a JSON schema check and re-test
Limit a lab web server's outbound connections with a firewall egress rule and store uploads outside the web root, then verify both with tests

schedule.title: Defence in depth and configuration
schedule.exercise: Audit a lab web app's headers, TLS and cookie settings with a checklist, and rank the fixes by risk reduced per hour of effort.

tasks.title: Check the response headers of a lab app, list which security headers are missing, and add HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and a frame control
Harden a lab web server by enabling modern TLS only, setting cookie flags and CORS rules, and returning generic error pages, then verify each
Scan a lab project's dependencies for known vulnerable versions, upgrade the two worst, and confirm the app's tests still pass

schedule.title: Secure lifecycle, testing and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write up the capstone: for a vulnerable lab app, list the findings with severity, show the exploit evidence, describe the fix, and prove each fix with a retest.

tasks.title: Run an automated scanner against a local lab app, export the findings, and confirm by hand which three are true positives
Prioritise a backlog of 15 findings for a three-person team with two weeks, choosing what to fix first, and score against the rubric
Attack a vulnerable lab application to find six flaws, remediate each in code, and write a regression test proving every fix holds
